title: Force Index refinements — non-blocking review follow-up from PR #185
description: Non-blocking finding from pr-reviewer's review of PR #185 (backend-force-index-refinements), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so it isn't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: `_is_force_index_spike`'s new asymmetric-multiplier selection (`backend/app/signals/triple_screen.py`, around the `multiplier = (... if not negative else ...)` expression at the end of the function) uses a double-negative (`not negative` / `else`) ternary. This is a minor style inconsistency with the sign-selection code a few lines above it in the same function, which explicitly comments that it deliberately avoids exactly this pattern ('Signed multiplier rather than an `if negative: ... else: ...` pair of sign checks... instead of forcing a reader through... double-negative branches'). Rewriting as `_FORCE_INDEX_SPIKE_STDEV_MULTIPLIER_BULLISH if negative else _FORCE_INDEX_SPIKE_STDEV_MULTIPLIER_BEARISH` would read more directly and match the function's own stated convention. Purely a readability nit -- verified correct via hand-computed test values, not a behavior bug. Fixed opportunistically in PR #185 itself (as part of fixing the blocking is_force_index_reversal_spike baseline-window bug in the same file) rather than as a separate change here.

decisions.decision: Closing this task with a JSON-only PR (no source change) rather than re-applying the fix. Full backend suite re-run clean (850 passed) as a sanity check before closing.
